bug_semantics: PublicKeyBundle.from_dict() in openssl_encrypt/modules/key_bundle.py deserializes untrusted JSON into a key bundle without verifying the ML-DSA self_signature, and to_identity() then converts that unverified bundle into an Identity. A caller that does from_dict() then to_identity() (or uses plugin fetch/cache paths that deserialize without verify) can encrypt to an attacker-controlled public key and leak plaintext. key_resolver.py does verify before to_identity, but the unguarded API remains directly callable. CWE-347; vendor GHSA-8h88-gxp3-j7pg; affected < 1.4.0 (1.4.0b* shipped the unguarded API), patched in 1.4.0.
flaw_origin: The unguarded deserialization path was first written in fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 (2025-12-30), which added openssl_encrypt/modules/key_bundle.py with from_dict() returning an unverified PublicKeyBundle (docstring: 'SECURITY: Does NOT verify signature. Call verify_signature() after creation.') and to_identity() with no verified-state check. The same commit also added in-tree callers PublicKeyBundle.from_dict() in plugins/keyserver/keyserver_plugin.py (_fetch_from_server, documented as unverified) and plugins/keyserver/cache.py. Immediate parent 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 has no key_bundle.py, no PublicKeyBundle class, and no to_identity(); only a design-doc sketch in keyserver_plan.md. No finer public member commits or PR history reconstruct the file add.
